I am 64 years old, and I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I know this land well — the soil is loamy but can get saline if I over-irrigate, and the spring winds can dry out the seedbed. With only my wife and me, I cannot chase after high-labor systems. Cotton is what this land is good for, and the gin in the county gives us a reliable buyer.

This year, I will plant all 9 mu to a single-season improved Bt cotton variety. I have seen too many neighbors lose money switching to new crops they do not understand. The Bt gene saves me labor on bollworm — at my age, I cannot crawl through the fields spraying every week like I did in the 1990s. I will rotary till in mid-April to break up the topsoil and warm the seedbed, then sow when the soil temperature steadies above 12°C. 

For fertilizer, I will apply about 20 kg nitrogen per mu total — half as compound fertilizer at planting, half as urea at flowering and boll-setting. I have learned that more nitrogen just makes the plants leggy and attracts aphids. I will add 8 kg phosphorus and 10 kg potassium per mu to keep the bolls full. My well gives me water, so I will irrigate four times: at sowing if the spring is dry, at early flowering, at peak boll-setting in August, and once in late August to finish the late bolls. I will spray pesticides three times — mainly for aphids and spider mites, since the Bt cotton handles the bollworm. I aim for 300 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year I got 280 kg; with good rain timing and my well, 300 kg is reasonable.
